title: Puppy Feeding Schedule: How Often to Feed Your Puppy (and When to Change)
description: How many times a day should a puppy eat? What AKC, VCA and Dogs Trust say about meals by age, portions, treats, water and switching to adult food.
excerpt: How often to feed a puppy by age, how to work out portions, and when to switch to adult food, from AKC, VCA and Dogs Trust.
seoTitle: Puppy Feeding Schedule: How Often to Feed by Age

html:
Most sources suggest small meals four times a day for a young puppy, three times a day from about 12 weeks, and two meals from about 6 months. They do not agree on every age, and VCA describes 2 to 3 meals a day for growing puppies. Follow the feeding guide on your puppy food, watch your puppy's body condition, and ask your vet before changing meal numbers.

Meals by age: what the sources say

SourceMeals per day
AKC6 to 12 weeks: 4. 3 to 6 months: 3. 6 to 12 months: 2.
Dogs TrustUnder 12 weeks: 4. From about 12 weeks: 3. From 6 months: 2.
VCAGenerally 2 to 3 times a day, in measured portions at regular times.
AKC (toy breeds)Under 4 months: 4 to 5. 4 to 7 months: 4. 7 to 9 months: 3. By 12 months: 2.
RSPCASmall, regular meals. No number given.

Dogs Trust says to speak to your vet before reducing your puppy's meals. Toy and small breeds may need more frequent meals than the general guide, so ask your vet.

How much to feed

  • Start with the packet. Dogs Trust says to check the food packet for the right amount, divide it across the day's meals, and adjust for your puppy's needs. The packet is a guide only.
  • Watch your puppy, not the bowl. AKC says body condition should decide portion sizes. It suggests weighing your puppy weekly and comparing the result with breed charts. Dogs Trust says to monitor weight and body condition.
  • Measure portions. VCA says portion feeding, with a controlled amount each day, is the best way to prevent puppies from becoming overweight. Free-choice feeding can raise the risk of extra body fat and, in large breeds, bone problems.
  • Do not guess grams. We found no source that gives one gram figure for all puppies. The right amount depends on the food, your puppy's age, size and activity, so your vet can help.

Choosing the food

  • Puppy food. AKC says growing puppies should be fed puppy food, and that adult food can rob them of important nutrients. VCA says to check the label for a statement that the food meets the requirements for growth. A food for all life stages is also appropriate.
  • Large breeds. VCA and AKC both say large-breed puppies need a food formulated for large-breed puppies.
  • No extra supplements. Both VCA and AKC say not to add vitamins or minerals without checking with your vet.
  • Keep the breeder's food at first. PDSA says to stick to the breeder's food and routine when your puppy settles in, and to change slowly over a couple of weeks.

An example day (illustrative only)

This is an example, not a prescription. Times, portions and meal numbers should match your puppy's age, breed and your vet's advice. It follows the four-meal pattern that AKC and Dogs Trust describe for young puppies.

Time (example)What happens
7:00Wake, potty, breakfast, potty
12:00Lunch, then potty
17:00Dinner, then potty
20:30Last small meal, then potty
22:00Bedtime potty

AKC and PDSA both say a puppy usually needs a bathroom break after meals. See our potty training schedule for how to fit it in. If you work all day, see puppy schedule when working full time.

Feeding routine tips

  • Same times each day. AKC says to feed at regular times in regular amounts.
  • Do not leave food down all day. AKC says not to leave food down for more than 15 minutes. Dogs Trust says most dogs should not have food left out all day, as it can spoil.
  • Skipped meal? If your puppy is not eating at mealtimes, speak to your vet (Dogs Trust).

Water

AKC and Dogs Trust both say your puppy should have fresh water available. Dogs Trust says to leave the bowl out and refill it. AKC has a separate article on housetraining that suggests removing the water bowl at night, which differs from this advice. Talk to your vet before limiting water, especially for small puppies.

Treats

Dogs Trust says treats should be no more than 10 percent of your dog's diet, and to reduce regular portions if needed. AKC gives the same 10 percent figure and says it is based on calories. Training treats count.

Changing food

  • Do it gradually. Sudden changes can cause digestive upset or diarrhea (AKC, Dogs Trust).
  • How long. AKC suggests 5 to 7 days: about 25 percent new food on day one, 50 percent on day three, 75 percent on day five, and 100 percent on day seven. Dogs Trust says a few days to a week.
  • Stomach upset. If it continues after a gradual change, call your vet (AKC).

When to switch to adult food

Sources do not give one age:

  • Dogs Trust: when your puppy has stopped growing, which varies by size and breed. Check the manufacturer's guidance and ask your vet.
  • AKC: small breeds around 7 to 9 months, larger breeds at 12 to 14 months. AKC says it is better to be on puppy food a little too long, and that spayed or neutered puppies may switch earlier.
  • VCA: small and medium breeds mature at about 10 to 12 months, and large and giant breeds at 18 to 24 months.

Ask your vet when to switch, and switch gradually.

Healthy growth

VCA says slow, steady growth is best. Too-rapid growth from high-energy foods or overfeeding raises the risk of skeletal problems and obesity, especially in large breeds. AKC says a young dog carrying too much weight has a higher risk of orthopedic problems. Dogs Trust says obesity raises the risk of arthritis, diabetes and heart disease.

When to ask your vet

  • Your puppy refuses food or has repeated vomiting or diarrhea
  • Your puppy seems too thin or too heavy
  • You want to change meal numbers, food type or switch to adult food
  • You have a toy or large breed puppy and are unsure about the schedule

This article is general information, not veterinary advice.

quick: Sources suggest about four meals a day for young puppies, three from around 12 weeks and two from around 6 months, though VCA describes 2 to 3. Follow the food's feeding guide, watch body condition, and ask your vet before changing meals or food.

faq.q: How many times a day should I feed my puppy?
faq.a: AKC and Dogs Trust say 4 meals for young puppies, then 3, then 2. VCA says 2 to 3 for growing puppies. Ask your vet.

faq.q: How much should I feed my puppy?
faq.a: Start with the packet's feeding guide and adjust to your puppy's body condition.

faq.q: Should I leave food out all day?
faq.a: Sources advise against it. VCA says free-choice feeding can increase the risk of excess weight.

faq.q: Can I give my puppy adult food?
faq.a: AKC says puppies should eat puppy food. A food for all life stages is also appropriate (VCA).

faq.q: When do I switch to adult food?
faq.a: It depends on size and breed. AKC suggests 7 to 9 months for small breeds and 12 to 14 months for larger breeds. Ask your vet.

faq.q: How many treats can a puppy have?
faq.a: No more than 10 percent of the daily diet, according to Dogs Trust and AKC.

faq.q: Should I take away my puppy's water at night?
